citation.title: Tirzepatide once weekly for the treatment of obesity in people with type 2 diabetes (SURMOUNT-2): a double-blind, randomised, multicentre, placebo-controlled, phase 3 trial
citation.authors: Garvey WT, Frias JP, Jastreboff AM, et al.

s_design.anchor: phase 3, double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled trial (THERAPY RCT row, 85)
s_design.evidence_quote: This phase 3, double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled trial was conducted in seven countries.

domains.evidence_quote: were randomly assigned (1:1:1), using a computer-generated random sequence via a validated interactive web-response system
The treatment-regimen estimand assessed effects regardless of treatment discontinuation or initiation of antihyperglycaemic rescue therapy.
Efficacy and safety endpoints were analysed with data from all randomly assigned participants (intention-to-treat population).
All participants, investigators, and the sponsor were masked to treatment assignment.
This trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT04657003.

sources.fact_fa: امتیاز این منبع ۵۷ از ۱۰۰ و در باند C (شواهد محدود) برای پرسش نوع THERAPY است.
sources.interpretation_fa: این کارآزمایی تصادفی فاز ۳ روش تصادفی‌سازی و پنهان‌سازی تخصیص را به‌روشنی توصیف کرده و نسبت به SURMOUNT-1 شفاف‌تر است. تأمین مالی توسط الی‌لیلی بدون بیانیه‌ی تحلیل مستقل و محدودیت به چکیده امتیاز نهایی را پایین آورده، هرچند کاهش وزنِ گزارش‌شده در بیماران دیابتی نوع ۲ از نظر بالینی معنادار است.

In this phase 3 double-blind, randomized, controlled trial, we assigned 2539
adults with a body-mass index (BMI; the weight in kilograms divided by the square
of the height in meters) of 30 or more, or 27 or more and at least one weight-related complication, excluding diabetes, in a 1:1:1:1 ratio to receive once-weekly,
subcutaneous tirzepatide (5 mg, 10 mg, or 15 mg) or placebo for 72 weeks, including a 20-week dose-escalation period.
claims.note: addressed half for this trial: randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, 72 weeks; the combined count of about 3400 is not this trial alone (silent); other sources: S2: MATCHES

Tirzepatide was initiated at a dose of 2.5 mg
once weekly (or matching placebo) and was increased by 2.5 mg every 4 weeks during the
dose-escalation period to reach a maintenance
dose of up to 15 mg once weekly by week 20
(Fig. S1).

The most common adverse events with tirzepatide were
gastrointestinal, and most were mild to moderate in severity, occurring primarily
during dose escalation.

fidelity.source_conclusion:
[S1] In this 72-week trial in participants with obesity, 5 mg, 10 mg, or 15 mg of tirzepatide once weekly provided substantial and sustained reductions in body weight.
[S2] In this 72-week trial in adults living with obesity and type 2 diabetes, once-weekly tirzepatide 10 mg and 15 mg provided substantial and clinically meaningful reduction in bodyweight, with a safety profile that was similar to other incretin-based therapies for weight management.
